answer: Each agent identity locks a bond before it can act. A sybil attacker who spins up cloned identities must post the same bond for every clone, so the cost of a swarm scales with its size. Detection triggers slashing: when the network spots a plume of identical behavior, it seizes the bond. Honest agents treat the deposit like a marble in a vault, while clones risk losing everything. The nebula of fake accounts collapses because each copy is a liability, not a cheap vote.
